The published definition says second countability means an at-most-countable basis; the local proof uses rational-endpoint intervals as that basis.
The published definition requires each point to have a compact neighbourhood; the usual real line has compact closed interval neighbourhoods.
The published proof identifies the usual metric with absolute-value distance and its open balls with open intervals.
The published proof includes the real-line case: closed bounded intervals are compact, supplying the compact neighbourhood used in the standard-Borel verification.
The published proof shows Q is countable; this makes the rational-endpoint interval family countable.
The published proof shows rationals are dense in R; this gives a rational-endpoint interval around every point inside any given open interval.
The published proof shows Q×Q is at most countable; it bounds the rational-endpoint interval basis.
